did_you_know.text: Did you know? According to the chapter, Israel was handed over to Midian for seven years because they did evil in the sight of the Lord.
Did you know? Because of Midian, the Israelites were forced to hide in tunnels, caves, and mountain strongholds to protect their possessions and crops.
Did you know? After the Israelites cried out, the Lord sent a prophet who reminded them of the Exodus from Egypt and their deliverance from their enemies, but also rebuked them for not obeying him.
Did you know? Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress rather than in an open place in order to hide the crop from Midian.
Did you know? The angel of the Lord addressed Gideon as a "mighty warrior," even though Gideon described his family as the weakest and himself as the youngest in his father’s household.
Did you know? After fire rose from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread, Gideon built an altar to the Lord and named it "The Lord Is Peace."
Did you know? Gideon tore down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah pole at night—not because he was disobedient, but because he was afraid of his father’s household and the people of the town.
Did you know? When the people of the town demanded that Gideon be put to death, Joash replied that if Baal was truly a god, he should defend his own altar.

Did you know? After Midian, Amalek, and the people of the east gathered in the Valley of Jezreel, the Spirit of the Lord clothed Gideon, and he blew a trumpet to summon the Abiezrites and the neighboring tribes.
Did you know? Gideon asked for two signs using a fleece: first, dew on the fleece alone while the ground remained dry, and then a dry fleece while dew covered all the ground. Both signs took place.
